To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a sound algorithm allows to trade off precision and efficiency, (2) the use of an incremental algorithm allows to trade efficiency for precision, (3) the use of sound incremental algorithms allows to trade off efficiency for precision, which is a very good trade-off.
we have proposed a sound lightweight formal scenario-based software engineering technique that scales well.

(1) the soundness of a model checking algorithm can be improved by adding a local consistency check; (2) this consistency check can be performed by using an automata-based approach, which is much more efficient than the usual one; (3) this consistency check, when applied to a synthesis algorithm, can be used to produce a more efficient and more precise algorithm; (4) the soundness and the efficiency can be improved by using an automaton-based approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a lightweight formal approach for the analysis of scenarios and state machines.
the following questions: - How can we make formal scenario synthesis and model checking efficient?
the development of efficient and precise techniques for synthesizing state machines from Live Sequence Charts, and vice-versa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can synthesize and verify LSCs with state machines, in an industrial scale, in reasonable time, and with a good precision, which is good enough for the purpose.
we can now do sound formal scenario synthesis and model checking in a matter of seconds, and that the resulting state machines are very close to the original scenarios.
our algorithms are fast, lightweight, and formal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach for the synthesis of state machines from Live Sequence Charts (LSCs), and a new approach for model checking LSCs against state machines.
we propose an algorithm to compute the set of states reachable from an initial state in a state machine.
the proposed algorithms are able to synthesise state machines for scenarios in the order of thousands, in a reasonable amount of time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the precision of the verification process can be adjusted, depending on the needs of the user.
soundness is a very useful feature to have, even at a cost of precision.
the loss of precision can be kept to a minimum, while the efficiency is improved.
